mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >2% YoY and HOUST drops >10% YoY simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators are strong (UNRATE > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals expanding supply capacity and robust economic activity, which supports higher corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises as specified but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 70% of instances, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 100k signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes Fed tightening and negative equity risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails outside of recession periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1% while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat signals weakening consumer demand without supply-side offset, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls >1% month-over-month AND INDPRO change is within [-0.2%, +0.2%]
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is rising rapidly (CPIAUCSL > YoY +0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200k for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate margin growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% signals synchronized supply expansion, which boosts earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 1% AND HOUST > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when monetary policy is restrictive (FEDFUNDS > 5%).
